info.title: NGP VAN API (community OpenAPI spec)
info.description:
Community-maintained OpenAPI spec for the NGP VAN API, reverse-engineered from https://docs.ngpvan.com, the NGPVAN/van-cli source, and live probing of the sandbox API. The spec describes the API's actual behavior as observed. Where that behavior deviates from the official docs, the comparison is recorded out of band in `x-docs-discrepancy` fields (hidden by most documentation renderers) and summarized in [DISCREPANCIES.md](https://github.com/NickCrews/van-openapi/blob/main/DISCREPANCIES.md); research evidence and confidence notes live in `x-provenance` fields.

Source repository: https://github.com/NickCrews/van-openapi — file issues and corrections there. This spec is not published or endorsed by NGP VAN; for questions about the API itself, contact APIDevelopers@ngpvan.com.

See [STATUS.md](https://github.com/NickCrews/van-openapi/blob/main/STATUS.md) for per-endpoint research status.

**The API is not callable from a browser.** Its CORS support is incomplete: `api.securevan.com` answers the preflight correctly — reflecting the request origin and allowing the `Authorization` header — but omits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` from the actual response (observed 2026-08-03; a `200` comes back with no `access-control-*` headers at all). A browser therefore sends the request, receives the response, and then blocks the page from reading it. `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` is missing as well, which Basic auth would separately require. This affects only browser-based callers; server-side clients such as cURL, Python, or Apps Script are unaffected, since CORS is enforced by the browser rather than the server.

get.summary: Get a person by VAN id
get.description: Retrieves a person record. Related collections (emails, phones, addresses, …) are null unless requested via $expand, and empty arrays when expanded but absent. An unknown, zero, or negative vanId returns the standard 404 error envelope; a non-integer path segment does not match the route and returns an HTML 404 page instead.

parameters.description: VAN id of the person.
parameters.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs type this path parameter as string (default "100476252"); the route only matches integers — a non-integer segment returns an IIS HTML 404 page (observed 2026-08-03).

parameters.name: $expand
parameters.description: Related sections to include, comma-delimited eg 'addresses,emails'. Anything outside this set returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with a hint listing the valid values. Two sections in the set are still refused in a My Campaign context: `scores` with 403 FORBIDDEN and `pollingLocation` with 400 BAD_REQUEST.

post.description:
Merges the payload into an existing record, addressed by id — no matching, no minimum-criteria threshold, and no chance of writing to the wrong duplicate. **This is the endpoint to write through once you have identified a person yourself** (e.g. from GET /people); POST /people/findOrCreate resolves ambiguity silently and creates duplicates below the match threshold.

Fields left out of the body keep their current values, and `emails`, `phones` and `addresses` are appended to what is already there rather than replacing it — there is no way to remove a contact method through this endpoint. The update is not idempotent for contact methods: sending the same email twice adds it twice.

Outcomes:

- **The vanId exists** — **302 Found** with a `Location` header pointing back at `/people/{vanId}` and a match-stub body: the same shape POST /people/find returns, **not** the updated record.
- **The body is empty (`{}`)** — accepted, answered the same **302**, and nothing changes.
- **An unknown, zero or negative vanId** — **404**.

x-provenance.note: Merge semantics confirmed by updating only middleName on a record and observing firstName, lastName and employer survive; append semantics by adding a second email and seeing both returned, with isPreferred moving to the newer one. Not in the official docs' page index; the path comes from van-cli (people.ts update), which notes PUT is not supported.

200.description:
Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* after a successful update:

```
POST /people/102714580         {"firstName": "Cre", …}
  ← 302 Found
    Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714580   (same URL)
    {"vanId": 102714580, "status": "Matched"}

GET /people/102714580          ← client re-issues the request at Location
  ← 200 OK
    { the merged record — the body documented here }
```

A happy accident: the update itself never returns the record, but the followed GET does, so redirect-following clients get the merged result for free. See POST /people/find for the full redirect-following notes, including the `curl -X POST -L` gotcha.

The other way to reach a 200 is a failure: when the 302 was the ASP.NET request-validation bounce (a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&`), following it lands on the web application's HTML error page, which answers 200 with `text/html`. Check the content type before parsing JSON.

x-provenance.note: Chain observed end to end with httpx: POST /people/{vanId} with an empty body → 302 back to the same URL → GET → 200 with the full record.

302.description:
The record was updated. `Location` points back at the person resource; the body is a match stub, not the updated record.

The same status also covers a failure that never reaches the API: a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&` is rejected by ASP.NET request validation and redirected to `/Error.aspx?EID={code}` with an HTML body. Check the content type to tell them apart.

Location.description: URL of the updated person — or of the web application's error page when request validation rejected the path.

x-provenance.note: "Object moved" body of the request-validation redirect; see the RequestValidationRedirect response for the full story.

getUpdatedPerson.description: Fetch the record to see the merged result — the update response does not include it.

get.description:
Searches for people matching the given criteria and returns full person records in the standard pagination envelope. At least one search parameter must be set: firstName, lastName, middleName, streetAddress, city, stateOrProvince, zipOrPostalCode, phoneNumber, email, commonName, or officialName. A request with none of these — even one with filter or paging parameters set — returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with the text "This endpoint requires at least one search parameter to be set." Text criteria are case-insensitive prefix matches: lastName=Testpers matches "Testperson", lastName=estperson does not. Related collections on the returned records are null unless requested via $expand.

**This is the endpoint to use when you only have loose criteria.** Unlike POST /people/find and POST /people/findOrCreate — which refuse to attempt a match until you supply one of a handful of minimum field combinations, and answer Unmatched (or create a duplicate) when you cannot — this search has no such threshold. A single name is a perfectly valid query. In exchange it makes no identity claim: it hands back every record whose fields start with what you typed, and deciding which one is your person, or that none of them is, is your job. Inspect the candidates (with $expand for addresses, emails and phones if you need them) and take the vanId from there.

x-provenance.source: van-cli people.ts (list command) plus live sandbox probing; the endpoint is absent from the official docs' page index (llms.txt lists only /people/find).

post.summary: Find a person matching the given criteria
post.description:
Attempts to match a person in the database. Read-only: never creates records (use POST /people/findOrCreate for that).

Outcomes:

- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — that record is returned as a **302** and every other criterion is ignored, no threshold involved.
- **One record matches** — **302 Found**, with a `Location` header pointing at `/people/{vanId}` and a small match-stub body, `{"vanId": …, "status": "Matched"}`.
- **Several records match** — still a **302** for exactly one of them, and nothing in the response says the match was ambiguous. Which one you get depends on the shape of the criteria; see **When more than one record matches** below.
- **Nothing matches** — **404** with `{"vanId": null, "status": "Unmatched"}` (a match stub, not the standard error envelope).
- **The criteria fall short of the minimum combination** — **404 Unmatched** as well, not a 400, and indistinguishable from a genuine no-match. This is the common case to guard against; see **The criteria must reach a minimum combination** below.

## The criteria must reach a minimum combination

This endpoint is deliberately conservative — it would rather return nothing than return the wrong person. It does not attempt a match at all until the criteria reach one of these combinations:

- first name + last name + **email address**
- first name + last name + **phone**
- first name + last name + **zip5** + **date of birth**
- first name + last name + **street number + street name + zip5**
- **email address** on its own (a **phone** on its own matches too, though the docs list only email)

Anything short of that — a name on its own, name + date of birth, name + zip — comes back **404 Unmatched** regardless of who is in the database.

**A 404 here does not mean the person does not exist.** It usually means you did not supply enough to identify them. Do not treat Unmatched as "not in the database", and in particular do not follow it with a create — see POST /people/findOrCreate, which silently creates a duplicate for exactly this reason.

**If all you have is a name, use GET /people instead.** That endpoint is a loose prefix search with no threshold: `GET /people?firstName=Match&lastName=Threshold` returns full records for every candidate, and you decide which one (if any) is your person by inspecting them. Use /people/find only once you hold a strong identifier.

## How the criteria are compared

- Everything you send must agree with the record. Adding a **wrong** first name to a correct email turns a match into Unmatched — extra criteria narrow, they never widen.
- Comparison is case- and format-insensitive: `MATCH.THRESHOLD@EXAMPLE.COM` matches the stored lowercase address, `907-555-4242` matches the stored `9075554242`, and per the docs it is accent-insensitive too ("Pérez" matches "Perez"). Names may match on nicknames and variants unless the context has "Disable Partial Matching" turned on.
- The address combination needs the street **number**: `742 Evergreen Terrace` + zip matched; `Evergreen Terrace` + the same zip did not. A wrong zip with a right street also fails.

## When more than one record matches

Duplicates are common in VAN databases, and this endpoint does not warn you about them: **it returns exactly one vanId with no indication that others also matched.** A 302 is not proof that the match was unique.

The pick is deterministic, but the tiebreak depends on the shape of the criteria — with three identical records (102719047 < 102719048 < 102720144, same name, email and phone):

- criteria **including a name** (name+email, name+phone, name+dob+zip) → always the **lowest vanId**, i.e. the oldest record
- criteria **without a name** (email alone, phone alone) → always the **highest vanId**, i.e. the newest record

It is not the best-matching record and not the most recently updated one: enriching the newer duplicate so it matched the criteria at least as fully did not move a name-based match off the oldest record, and touching either record changed nothing.

The consequence to plan for: at the threshold you may be handed a stale or partial duplicate, and a follow-up write through POST /people/{vanId} then lands on whichever record won the tiebreak while the other keeps drifting. When it matters that you have *the* record rather than *a* record, list the candidates with GET /people and reconcile them yourself.
post.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs imply a 200 with a person object on match. Sandbox probing (2026-08-03) shows 302 + Location on match and 404 with a match stub on no match; no 400 was observed even for sparse criteria like firstName-only. Criteria below the documented minimum combinations are also answered 404 Unmatched rather than rejected, so under-specified requests are indistinguishable from genuine no-matches. The docs are also silent on ambiguous matches: when several records satisfy the criteria the API returns one of them with no indication that others matched.

x-provenance.note: Minimum combinations taken from the docs' Match Candidate common model (https://docs.ngpvan.com/reference/common-models) and confirmed one by one against a purpose-built sandbox record (vanId 102719047: Match Threshold, dob 1980-04-15, match.threshold@example.com, 9075554242, 742 Evergreen Terrace / 99501). Unmatched: lastName alone; firstName+lastName; firstName+lastName+dateOfBirth; firstName+lastName+zip; firstName+lastName+street-name-without-number+zip; firstName+lastName+street+wrong zip; wrong firstName + correct email. Matched: email alone; phone alone; name+email; name+phone; name+dob+zip; name+street+zip; uppercased email; phone with dashes; miscased names. Ambiguous-match behavior probed 2026-08-04 with three deliberately identical records (102719047, 102719048, 102720144 — same name, email and phone): exactly one vanId is returned with no ambiguity signal; name-bearing criteria always returned the lowest vanId and name-less criteria (email alone, phone alone) always the highest, across repeated runs, after touching either record, and after enriching the newer duplicate to match the criteria as fully as the older one.

200.description:
Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* on a match:

```
POST /people/find              {"firstName": "Ada", "lastName": "Testperson", …}
  ← 302 Found
    Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714507
    {"vanId": 102714507, "status": "Matched"}

GET /people/102714507          ← client re-issues the request at Location
  ← 200 OK
    { full person record — the body documented here }
```

requests, httpx, fetch and `curl -L` all follow that redirect and downgrade POST to GET by default, so a match reaches your code as this 200 and a full `Person`, never as the 302 and its two-field match stub. The no-match 404 is not a redirect, so the practical test is `resp.status_code == 200` vs `404`, not `302` vs `404`. The follow-up GET has no `$expand`, so its related collections come back null — re-fetch through the `getMatchedPerson` link if you need addresses, phones or emails.

Gotcha: `curl -X POST -L` keeps the method across the redirect and re-POSTs to `/people/{vanId}` — the *update* endpoint — where IIS answers `411 Length Required` because the re-issued request carries no body. Drop the explicit `-X POST` (`-d` already implies POST) and curl downgrades to GET like everything else.

x-provenance.note: Chain observed end to end with httpx and requests (both: 302 → GET → 200 Person) and with curl 8.7.1 both ways (`-d` alone → GET → 200; `-X POST -L` → POST /people/{vanId} → 411). Documented alongside the raw 302 so both redirect-following clients and raw clients (including the schemathesis fuzzer) conform to this spec.

302.description: A person matched the criteria. `Location` header points at the canonical person resource.

getMatchedPerson.description: Fetch the matched person's full record — equivalent to following the Location header.

404.description:
No person matched the criteria. Body is a match stub with status "Unmatched" (NOT the standard error envelope).

This is also the answer when the criteria never reached the minimum combination needed to attempt a match at all — there is no 400 and nothing in the body distinguishes the two cases. **Read it as "not identified", not "not in the database":** a person you can see through GET /people will still come back Unmatched here if all you sent was their name. See the operation description for the combinations that do trigger a match.

post.summary: Find a person, or create one if nothing matches
post.description:
Runs the same match as POST /people/find and, when nothing matches, stores the payload as a new record.

Outcomes:

- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — the match is short-circuited, that record is returned as **302 Found**, and nothing is created.
- **One record matches** — **302 Found**, with a `Location` header and `{"vanId": …, "status": "Matched"}`.
- **Several records match** — still a **302** for exactly one of them, with nothing in the response to say the match was ambiguous. See POST /people/find for which one you get.
- **Nothing matches** — **201 Created** with `{"vanId": …, "status": "UnmatchedStored"}`, and the payload is stored as a new record. Unlike find, this never returns 404 — the no-match case is the create case.
- **The criteria fall short of the minimum combination** — **201 Created** as well: a brand-new record, even when the person is already in the database. This is the duplicate trap; see **The match half has a minimum threshold** below.
- **The body is empty (`{}`)** — every field is optional, including the name, so this is a no-match: **201** and a blank record is created.

## The match half has a minimum threshold — below it, you create duplicates

The match runs under the same rules as POST /people/find: nothing is searched until the payload reaches one of these combinations:

- first name + last name + **email address**
- first name + last name + **phone**
- first name + last name + **zip5** + **date of birth**
- first name + last name + **street number + street name + zip5**
- **email address** on its own (a **phone** on its own works too)

**Below the threshold there is no "unmatched" to inspect — the API just creates a second record.** Posting `{"firstName": "Match", "lastName": "Threshold"}` for a person who is already in the database returns 201 with a fresh vanId, and the two records now both exist. This is the main way duplicate records get into a VAN database through the API.

So: only send a payload here that carries a strong identifier. If all you have is a name, search with GET /people first, decide for yourself whether a candidate is your person, and update it by id through POST /people/{vanId} instead.

x-provenance.note: Not in the official docs' page index; the path comes from van-cli (people.ts findOrCreate), which requires firstName and lastName client-side. The API itself requires neither — an empty body was accepted (observed 2026-08-03). Threshold behavior confirmed 2026-08-04: firstName+lastName for existing vanId 102719047 created duplicate 102719048 (201 UnmatchedStored); the same name plus the record's email returned 302 Matched.

post.x-docs-discrepancy: The docs present the minimum match combinations as a matching quality note; in practice, on this endpoint, falling short of them is what silently produces duplicate records (observed 2026-08-04).

post.description:
Stores the payload as a new record. **No de-duplication happens**: posting a name and email identical to an existing record creates a second record. Use POST /people/findOrCreate when you want matching — bearing in mind that it too creates a second record unless your payload reaches the minimum match combination documented there (name alone never does).

Outcomes:

- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — nothing is created and that record is returned as **302 Found**, exactly as findOrCreate would answer. This is the only way this endpoint declines to create a record.
- **Anything else** — **201 Created** with `{"vanId": …, "status": "Stored"}`. A payload identical to an existing person is not a special case: it creates a duplicate.
- **The body is empty (`{}`)** — every field is optional, so this too returns **201**, creating a blank record with no name.

get.description:
Returns the person's notes in the standard pagination envelope.

View-restricted notes are withheld from API keys: a note saved with `isViewRestricted: true` is absent from `items` and is not counted in `count`, so every note in the response has `isViewRestricted` false. `contactHistory` is always null, even for a note created with one, and `$expand=noteDetails` — the only value the parameter accepts — returns a byte-identical body.

Items come back oldest first by `createdDate`, ties broken by descending `noteId`. `$orderby` is validated against its two allowed properties but has no observable effect: `CreatedDate desc` returns the same order as the default.

An unknown, zero or negative vanId returns the standard 404 envelope; a non-integer path segment matches no route and returns an HTML 404 page.

parameters.name: vanId
parameters.description: VAN id of the person.
parameters.x-docs-discrepancy: Official docs type this path parameter as string (default "100476252"); the route only matches integers — a non-integer segment returns an IIS HTML 404 page (observed 2026-08-04).

parameters.name: $top
parameters.description: Limits the number of results. Default 25, maximum 50. A value of 0 or less returns 400; so does a non-numeric value, with the same message as an over-maximum one.

parameters.name: $skip
parameters.description: Number of results to skip. Must be 0 or greater.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description: Accepted but ignored. The API validates the value — only `CreatedDate` and `IsPinned` pass, case-insensitively, optionally followed by ` desc` — and then returns the default order regardless, including for `desc`.

x-provenance.note: Valid values come from the API's own INVALID_PARAMETER hint on `$orderby=noteId`. All four accepted values, plus `createddate` in lower case, returned an identical item order on a person with six notes.

parameters.name: $expand
parameters.description: `noteDetails` is the only value the API accepts; anything else returns 400 INVALID_PARAMETER with a hint saying so. Expanding has no observable effect — the response is identical with and without it, `contactHistory` included.

post.description:
Creates a note on the person.

On success the response is **204 No Content** with an empty body: the new `noteId` is not returned and there is no `Location` header, so the only way to learn it is to read the notes back. Two notes with identical text are two separate records — the endpoint is not idempotent.

`isPinned` is accepted and ignored; notes always read back `isPinned: false`. Unknown fields are ignored too. A `contactHistory` object records a Contact History entry alongside the note, but the note's own `contactHistory` stays null in every response.

A note saved with `isViewRestricted: true` can be written but never read back through the API — it is excluded from `GET /people/{vanId}/notes` and from `$expand=notes` on the person.

Updates an existing note. Only `text`, `isViewRestricted` and `category` can be changed; `isPinned` and the note's contact history cannot.

**This action is restricted for the key used to research this spec.** Every request returns 403 FORBIDDEN "Access to this action is restricted", whether or not the note exists, so the success path has not been observed live — the request body and the 204 below come from the official docs. `GET` and `DELETE` on this same path are restricted the same way; they are left out of this spec because their success shapes are unknown and undocumented.

PUT with a valid body against a real note (184579 on vanId 102714507) and against a nonexistent noteId both returned 403, so the restriction is applied before the note is looked up. The 204 success response is from https://docs.ngpvan.com/reference/peoplevanidnotesnoteid — not yet observed live.

Returns every note category available in the current context as a **bare JSON array** — this endpoint does not use the pagination envelope, and it ignores query parameters such as `$top`.

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic auth. Username = an arbitrary label, e.g. `my_fancy_app`; password = `{apiKey}|{databaseMode}` where databaseMode is `0` (My Voters) or `1` (My Campaign) and apiKey is a UUID like `07540886-b749-433c-b18d-a3d052f6b759`. ActionRestricted.description:
The API key's profile does not permit this action at all. The body carries nothing beyond the code, and the check runs before the target is looked up, so a restricted action answers 403 even for an id that does not exist — which also means a 403 here says nothing about whether the record is there.

Distinct from the other 403 in this spec: that one refuses a particular *section* of an otherwise-allowed request (`$expand=scores` from a My Campaign key), while this one refuses the whole operation.

x-provenance.note: Observed on GET, PUT and DELETE of /people/{vanId}/notes/{noteId} and on DELETE /people/{vanId} with the research key, while GET and POST of /people/{vanId}/notes work normally. Whether any key in the sandbox committee is granted these actions is unknown, so the success paths behind this response are unverified.

QueryStringTooLong.description: The request never reached the API. IIS rejects any request whose query string runs past roughly 2048 characters and answers with its own HTML "404 - File or directory not found" page, so this 404 means the URL was too long rather than that anything was missing. Nothing in the body identifies the real cause; check the content type, since the API's own 404s are JSON.

PersonNotFound.description: No person with that vanId exists. Zero and negative ids return this too, as the standard error envelope. RequestValidationRedirect.description:
The request never reached the API. ASP.NET request validation rejects a path segment containing `<`, `>`, `*` or `&` and hands the request to the VAN web application, which answers **302** with `Location: /Error.aspx?EID={code}` and a small HTML "Object moved" body. Clients that follow the redirect land on the web app's HTML "Oops...something went wrong" page with status 200 — HTML, not JSON, from an endpoint that otherwise only speaks JSON.

Other unusual path characters take different routes: `:` and `"` give the IIS HTML 404, and a backslash gives the standard JSON 404 envelope.

x-provenance.note: Found by the stateful fuzz phase on GET /people/{vanId} and reproduced character by character. The EID in the Location is a support reference code; no request data is echoed back.

Location.description: The web application's error page, e.g. /Error.aspx?EID=26B226-343EF8

BadRequest.description:
Validation error, as the standard JSON envelope.

Two unrelated cases share this status and answer with `text/html` instead, because the request is rejected in front of the API and never reaches it: a percent-encoded control character such as `%7F` in the path gets IIS's "Bad Request - Invalid URL" page, and `%00` gets Cloudflare's "400 Bad Request" page. Check the content type before parsing.

ServerError.description: Internal server error. The API returns 500 (not 400) for various malformed inputs, e.g. negative delayInMilliseconds on /echoes, non-ASCII filter values on /surveyQuestions, vanId 0 or null phone entries on /people/find, a null phone entry on the person write endpoints, and an `identifiers` entry with the valid type `dwid` on POST /people/create. PersonMatchCriteria.description:
Match criteria. Every field is optional in the sense that the API never rejects a sparse body — but matching only happens once the criteria reach one of these minimum combinations:

- firstName + lastName + emails[].email
- firstName + lastName + phones[].phoneNumber
- firstName + lastName + addresses[].zipOrPostalCode (zip5) + dateOfBirth
- firstName + lastName + addresses[].addressLine1 (street number **and** street name) + addresses[].zipOrPostalCode (zip5)
- emails[].email on its own (phones[].phoneNumber on its own also works)

Below that, the request is answered Unmatched without a search rather than rejected. A valid vanId overrides all other criteria and skips the threshold entirely.

x-provenance.note: Combination list from the docs' Match Candidate common model, each combination confirmed against sandbox vanId 102719047 (see the x-provenance on POST /people/find for the full matched/unmatched probe list). `addresses` is absent from the docs' find request example but is accepted and is the only way to supply zip5 or a street address as criteria — name + dob + zip matched, name + dob alone did not.

vanId.description: VAN id of the person; a valid vanId overrides all other criteria and is looked up directly, with no minimum-combination threshold. Warning: the API returns 500 for vanId 0.

firstName.description: Required by every combination except the email-only (or phone-only) one. Compared case- and accent-insensitively, and may match nicknames and variants unless the context has "Disable Partial Matching" enabled. A first name that disagrees with the record turns an otherwise-matching request into Unmatched.

middleName.description: Never part of a minimum combination; only narrows a match that the other criteria already reached.

lastName.description: Required by every combination except the email-only (or phone-only) one. Same comparison rules as firstName.

dateOfBirth.description: Only reaches the threshold in combination with firstName, lastName and a zip5 in addresses[]. Name + dateOfBirth alone returns Unmatched.

emails.description: Email addresses to match on. The strongest single criterion: an address on its own reaches the threshold, no name required. Compared case-insensitively.

phones.description: Phone numbers to match on. Reaches the threshold with firstName + lastName, and — undocumented but observed — on its own as well. Punctuation is ignored: "907-555-4242" matches a stored "9075554242". A null array entry returns 500.
phones.x-docs-discrepancy: The docs list only an email address as a criterion sufficient on its own; a phone number alone also matched (observed 2026-08-04, sandbox vanId 102719047).

addresses.description: Addresses to match on — the only way to supply the zip5 that two of the minimum combinations require. Never sufficient on its own, and never with a name alone: firstName + lastName + zipOrPostalCode returns Unmatched unless a dateOfBirth or a street address comes with it. Unlike phones, a null array entry is tolerated (404 Unmatched, not 500).

PersonMatchAddress.description: An address used as match criteria — the fields the matcher reads, unlike the fuller PersonAddressInput used when writing. Only two shapes reach the matching threshold, both alongside firstName and lastName: zipOrPostalCode + dateOfBirth, or addressLine1 + zipOrPostalCode.

x-provenance.note: Accepted by POST /people/find and confirmed to drive matching against sandbox vanId 102719047 (742 Evergreen Terrace, Springfield AK 99501): name+dob+zip and name+addressLine1+zip both matched; name+zip alone, name+"Evergreen Terrace" (no street number)+zip, and name+addressLine1+wrong zip all returned Unmatched. Only these fields were probed as criteria; the write model's other fields (addressLine2/3, type, …) are accepted but were not observed to affect the outcome.

addressLine1.description: Street address. Must carry both the street **number** and the street name to count toward a match: "742 Evergreen Terrace" matched, "Evergreen Terrace" did not.

city.description: City or town. Not part of any minimum combination.

stateOrProvince.description: Two or three character state or province code, e.g. "MN", "ON", "NSW". Not part of any minimum combination.

zipOrPostalCode.description: The zip5 that the date-of-birth and street-address combinations both require. Must agree with the record — a right street with a wrong zip does not match.

countryCode.description: Two character ISO country code supported by the VAN context. Defaults to the context's country.

PersonMatchEmail.description: An email address used as match criteria — the address only, unlike the fuller PersonEmailInput used when writing.

PersonMatchPhone.description: A phone number used as match criteria — no type or opt-in fields, unlike the PersonPhoneInput used when writing.
